title: New apiserver subpackages must be listed in enterprise_imports.go
answers: Why doesn't the enterprise build pick up my new pkg/services/apiserver subpackage?
What else do I need to touch when adding a new package under pkg/services/apiserver that enterprise code depends on?
body:
Symptom: an enterprise extension (built with -tags enterprise) fails to see a new package under pkg/services/apiserver (e.g. keysroutes) even though it compiles in grafana/grafana itself.
Root cause: pkg/extensions/enterprise_imports.go maintains an explicit blank-import list of apiserver subpackages used by the enterprise overlay; a package missing from that list isn't wired into the enterprise build graph.
Fix pattern: add `_ "github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/services/apiserver/<newpkg>"` to pkg/extensions/enterprise_imports.go whenever a new apiserver subpackage (route builder, client, options, etc.) is introduced for enterprise consumption.
Constraints: only needed for packages the enterprise overlay actually imports; verify by building `-tags enterprise` with the enterprise source overlaid, since OSS CI alone won't catch a missing entry.
applies: pkg/extensions/enterprise_imports.go whenever adding a pkg/services/apiserver subpackage consumed by grafana-enterprise

search: Enterprise build wiring for apiserver subpackages: new packages under pkg/services/apiserver must be added as blank imports to pkg/extensions/enterprise_imports.go whenever consumed by grafana-enterprise, or the enterprise build will fail to see them despite OSS compilation succeeding. The fix is `_ "github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/services/apiserver/<newpkg>"` in that file. Only packages actually imported by enterprise overlay need this; verify by building with `-tags enterprise` and enterprise source overlaid, since OSS CI alone cannot detect missing entries.
